scenario: a second start() arms a second tick interval, and stop() leaves one running
reason: Owner-approved 2026-11-01 (decisions page row s): in 1.35 every start() arms a new tick interval, even while the system is running or after destroy(), and keeps only the newest handle, so ticks multiply and an older interval keeps firing after stop() or destroy(); 2.0 arms the tick only on a start() that starts the system, and stop() and destroy() clear it. In this scenario a second start() while running, then stop(), destroy() and start() again are followed by clock advances; 1.35 keeps extra tick intervals firing (more ticks, and a timer still pending after destroy()), 2.0 ticks once per running period and nothing after stop() or destroy(). This covers the scenario's "tick" record, where the value at data[2] differs in step 2. scenario: a batch that satisfied A by its own write, with A raised again while it runs: A completes twice, from the old batch and the new run, with no cancel (au)
kind: the batch [A, B] has satisfied both (30 ms)
reason: Row (as) (L7; owner-approved 2026-11-05, "Approve (Recommended)"): settle(), the settled notification and inspect() count a running batch, so settle() waits for batched work and inspect() lists a running batch's requirements in flight. 1.35 resolves settle() without waiting for the batches it started and lists no batch in flight (L7 RFC C6, probe B7). The approved risks: a fake-timer test that awaits settle() during a batch wait waits until the timers advance, and a batch longer than 5 s with no timeoutMs makes settle() reject. In this scenario the batch [A, B] satisfies A by its own write and A is raised again while the batch runs: 2.0's old batch reports a cancel for A when A's new run supersedes it, and A completes once, from the new run; 1.35 reports no cancel and completes A twice, once from the old batch (the records 2.0 lacks) and once from the new run. This record is one of the checkpoint's inspect() fields, taken while a batch runs: 2.0 lists the batch's requirements in flight (inflight and resolvers), 1.35 lists none. This covers the state "the batch [A, B] has satisfied both (30 ms)" record in step 2, which differs at inspect.inflight[0]. Signed 2026-11-05 on the owner's instruction: he approved this row ("Approve (Recommended)", 2026-11-05) and asked Claude to sign for him.

scenario: retracting one requirement of a running batch cancels all of it, and the still-wanted ones never run again (U2)
reason: Row (as) (L7; owner-approved 2026-11-05, "Approve (Recommended)"): settle(), the settled notification and inspect() count a running batch, so settle() waits for batched work and inspect() lists a running batch's requirements in flight. 1.35 resolves settle() without waiting for the batches it started and lists no batch in flight (L7 RFC C6, probe B7). The approved risks: a fake-timer test that awaits settle() during a batch wait waits until the timers advance, and a batch longer than 5 s with no timeoutMs makes settle() reject. In this scenario b is retracted from the running batch [a, b, c] at 30 ms: 2.0 cancels b alone, the signal stays clean, and a and c complete at 70 ms. This record is one of the checkpoint's inspect() fields, taken while a batch runs: 2.0 lists the batch's requirements in flight (inflight and resolvers), 1.35 lists none. This covers the state "running" record in step 3, which differs at inspect.inflight[0]. Signed 2026-11-05 on the owner's instruction: he approved this row ("Approve (Recommended)", 2026-11-05) and asked Claude to sign for him.

In this scenario (U11: a with-results batch whose items always fail, 2 attempts, no backoff, 10 ms; onResolverError "retry-later", delayMs 50, maxRetries 1) 2.0 retries the batch at 20 ms under quirk h and the error boundary hears a and b once each; then row p re-dispatches the requirements after the delay, and the re-dispatched batch retries once and errors once. 1.35 runs the batch twice at 10 ms, the boundary hears each item twice, and nothing runs again. These are the re-dispatch's records, which 2.0 already had before quirk h was built (L7a); where quirk h's entry for the same record class has used its count, the rest fall to this entry. This covers the external "call" record in step 4, which only 2.0 records. Signed 2026-11-05 on the owner's instruction: he approved this row ("If all are better or non user facing they are all approved", 2026-11-01) and asked Claude to sign for him.

scenario: the resolve() fallback's runs ignore a retraction: nothing is canceled and all three complete (U8)
